fact: The catalogue note on the Interior ministry's Q3 FY2025/26 execution report lists 30 communes digitalised in communal revenue, with the digitalisation of collection being extended; no total of communes is given and the document dates only by its 2026-07 publication.

The Interior ministry's FY2025/26 revised budget carries a 2,000,000,000 BIF line for extending the digitalisation of revenue collection in the communes, with execution columns empty in the filed workbook.
The record gives the origin of the 2,000,000,000 BIF line for extending communal revenue digitalisation as the domestic state budget.
The spending entity on the communal revenue digitalisation line is the Ministry of the Interior, Community Development and Public Security.

A headline listed on the Association des Communes du Burundi page names 12 communes (Bubanza, Bukinanyana, Kayanza, Ngozi, Kirundo, Muyinga, Cankuzo, Ruyigi, Rutana, Gitega, Makamba, Nyanza) as pilots for E-TAXE digital taxation for communal revenue management; the headline carries no date, so the page's 2026-02-09 date is used.

The national digitalisation master plan PDDSP 2023-2033, adopted by the Council of Ministers on 10 May 2023, includes an initiative to digitalise communal tax collection, run by the communal administrator with the public treasury and transacting from mobile terminals.
Kayanza commune's administrator said the e-Taxe application was introduced into the commune's tax collection; what it records is not stated.

Only Kayanza commune is named as collecting with the e-Taxe application; the article gives no total of communes using it (Burundi has no count stated here); in Ruyigi, traders pay communal taxes by mobile phone because no Bancobu branch is near the market.
Interbank Burundi said the IBB M+ platform had succeeded in Rumonge and Bujumbura Mairie in 2023; no total of communes is given.
Butihinda commune trained its planning, accounting and zonal accounting staff on IBB M+ on 5 May 2026; effective use is to start with the 2026-2027 budget year.

IBB M+ takes payments from traders by phone or from agents who convert cash to electronic money paid into the commune's account, with a notification per transaction to a commune officer, and keeps the data to follow revenue.
The platform is run by Interbank Burundi, a bank, with its call centre and agents; in areas without internet, such as Masaka zone, the classic collection system continues until further notice.
Butihinda commune held a training on IBB M+ on 5 May 2026 ahead of use from the 2026-2027 budget year.
Kayanza's accountant said 48 of the commune's 54 collectors use POS machines to collect, with the revenue transferred digitally to the commune's account and staff only monitoring.
Only Kayanza commune is named with POS collection (48 of its 54 collectors); no count of communes is given.
UNDP's mission of 16-20 June 2025 reported the E-Taxe system operational in communes such as Kayanza; only Kayanza is named and no total is given.
UNDP states that E-Taxe digitalises the collection of communal taxes in Kayanza; what it records is not stated.

The notice states the Direction of Communal Finances is considering an IT solution to replace the current system of manual collection of communal taxes; undated, so the notice's year 2021 (inferred from the mission window) is used.

The notice calls for a study across all 119 communes to establish, among other things, whether each has communal-tax software, and states no commune with a system; the current system is described as manual collection (notice dated 2021 by inference).
The Ministry of the Interior's Direction of Communal Finances envisages acquiring an IT system for communal revenue; UNDP funds only a feasibility study (mission 15 August to 15 December 2021).
